title: Rental platform fast-lane for protected tenants without exposing victim status to agents
moment: A protected tenant using a Taiwanese rental listing platform or a social-housing application wants the platform's fee waiver and the quick-move option offered to people leaving violent homes. Today she must upload her order or a social-worker letter to the platform's support staff, and the agent on the other end can see everything and she cannot be sure who else does.
verifier: Rental platform operator or social-housing application desk granting a fee waiver and priority
predicate: Applicant is covered by an active protection order during the lease-signing and move-in window
disclosed_today: Uploaded protection order scan or social worker letter, plus ID card images, visible to customer service staff and stored in the support ticket system
issuer: Local government social affairs bureau (domestic violence and sexual assault prevention center), attesting from the court order
why_zk: The platform wants only to apply a benefit rule, so a time-bounded 'covered now' proof is enough and avoids creating a database of victims. A second benefit is that a copied or stolen ID number is not enough, since the proof is bound to the holder's wallet, which addresses the weakness of identity checks that rely on easy-to-copy identifiers. Weakness: the benefit is small, the platform may not have an incentive to build verification, and the municipality would have to operate an issuing service.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the telco fraud case, the check relied on an ID number and issue date that were easy to copy, so a stolen identity passed; here, a wallet-bound signed claim from the bureau plays the stronger check in place of copyable document scans.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A provider must verify that a new applicant is the named person, but its check uses identifiers that are easy to copy, so a stolen identity passes and the real person bears the consequences. | mechanism: None; online verification only checked ID number and issue date.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In Korea's mobile licence age check, a scan at the counter is meant to yield only the age result rather than the whole card; here, a scan at the platform or housing desk yields only the 'covered now' result rather than the order.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A shop must confirm that a buyer is above an age threshold, but the buyer's credential shows the full photo and card details to the cashier, not just the age result. | mechanism: QR or barcode scan from the wallet app for age verification at the counter; the age result, not the full card, is the intended output.

title: Foreign-resident heir proves entitlement through a local agent without the agent seeing the full family tree
moment: A Taiwanese man dies leaving funds at a Cathay United branch; his daughter lives in Canada and appoints her uncle in Taipei as agent to collect her share. The bank wants the agent's full ID copy, a power of attorney, the heir's passport copy, and the full 繼承系統表 showing every relative, so the uncle holds a document about the whole family. The bank only needs to know that the principal heir is entitled to at least a stated share, and that the person appearing is her authorized agent.
verifier: Bank branch handling a cross-border estate claim via an agent (代理人)
predicate: Principal is an heir with entitlement >= stated share of decedent X's deposits AND the presenter is the designated agent of that heir, shown without disclosing other heirs
disclosed_today: Agent's national ID copy, heir's passport copy, full inheritance chart, notarized/consularly authenticated power of attorney, full names and relationships of all family members
issuer: Household registration office for the entitlement credential, plus the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (or the heir herself, as a peer) for the delegation credential
why_zk: The agent needs to carry a proof, not a copy of the family chart: a delegated-credential proof says 'this person is acting for an heir entitled to >= threshold', so the uncle and bank clerks never see siblings or other relatives. This mirrors the problem of the foreign investor's local agent who hands over a full ID copy. Weakness: consular authentication and wet-ink powers of attorney are mandated by law and practice, and the issuance of a delegation credential by a foreign resident would need new infrastructure.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the securities rule, a domestic agent for a foreign investor hands over a full ID copy to prove they are a real person; here, the Taipei uncle acting for his Canadian niece plays that role, and a delegated entitlement proof replaces the ID copy and the whole family chart.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A foreign investor must prove that its local agent is a real, identified person, and the agent hands over a full copy of an ID card, with no alternative verification stated. | mechanism: None stated; full ID copy required with no less-intrusive alternative given.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In onion routing, no single intermediary holds both origin identity and final destination; here, the agent holds only the delegated proof and the bank holds only the share threshold, so neither intermediary holds the heir's identity together with the family tree.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A route must be relayed through intermediaries so that no single intermediary holds both the origin identity and the final destination, while the traffic still reaches the endpoint. | mechanism: Onion routing, where the message is wrapped in one encryption layer per relay, and each relay peels only its own layer and passes the rest to the next hop.

title: Student discount on a library-linked reading-room pass without exposing the lending record
moment: A public library in a New Taipei district offers a free cross-branch study-room booking and a municipal reading-benefit points scheme to patrons in good standing. To enrol, the patron shows the library card, and the front desk looks up the full account, including every title borrowed and any fine history, to confirm nothing is overdue anywhere in the city network.
verifier: Municipal public library branch running the study-room and points programme
predicate: Not on the network-wide overdue or lost-item list (non-membership), proven at the time of booking
disclosed_today: Library card number, name, phone, and full lending history visible to the clerk, including titles that reveal health, religion or sexuality interests
issuer: The municipal library system's central circulation service, issuing a re-randomisable good-standing credential to each patron's phone
why_zk: Titles borrowed are sensitive, yet the clerk needs only to know there is no overdue or lost item anywhere in the network. A non-membership proof removes the clerk's view of reading history. It is moderately strong, since the issuer is a single public body that could instead simply return a yes or no to the branch. The honest weakness is that a plain server-side yes or no already solves most of this, and ZK only adds value if the clerk must not learn who the patron is, which is rarely required for a named study-room booking.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Title 13 census rule, staff can see raw records but nothing may be published that singles out a respondent; here, the proof plays that role by letting the clerk act on a network-wide result while the underlying lending records stay unseen.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: An agency holding individual responses must release aggregate results, and the legal duty bars any output from which a particular respondent can be singled out, while the holder's staff can still see the raw records. | mechanism: Statutory use limitation and publication prohibition enforced by sworn-oath duties and penalties; statistical disclosure limitation (for example differential privacy in later census products) is a technical layer not specified in the statute.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In SameSite cookies, a stored credential is sent only to the party it was issued for so third parties cannot match the holder across contexts; here, an unlinkable per-presentation proof plays that role so the study-room desk and the points scheme cannot link the same patron across visits.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A stored credential should be presented only to the party that issued it in the current context, but the browser sends it on any request the context triggers, so an unrelated observer can match the holder across contexts. | mechanism: The SameSite cookie attribute, which limits the cookie to same-site requests (Strict, Lax, or None); the IETF draft describes it as a per-cookie setting, and cross-site behaviour depends on the chosen value.

title: Several heirs each claim their own slice, and the bank stops keeping a full copy of the family tree in each file
moment: Four siblings agree to withdraw their late mother's NT$800k from a post office savings account in separate slices over several weeks. Each time, the clerk photocopies the full family chart and transcripts and keeps them in the case file, so by the end the bank holds four copies of the same sensitive tree in four files and any staff member can read them. The bank, under its AML recordkeeping duty, must retain evidence of why it paid each person, but only needs the entitlement fact.
verifier: Chunghwa Post branch (or a bank's estate-settlement back office) handling staged payouts to multiple heirs and retaining case records
predicate: Each claimant is an heir of decedent X entitled to >= their claimed payout fraction, with a verifiable proof retained instead of the family tree, and sum of claimed shares not exceeding 1
disclosed_today: Full inheritance chart and registry transcripts copied and retained in each claimant's file, ID copies of every heir, addresses, family relationships
issuer: Household registration office, with the bank's estate desk acting as an aggregator that checks the shares add up without seeing the tree
why_zk: Retention is the real harm: the bank must keep records for AML and audit, and a stored proof plus a share commitment satisfies auditors without keeping the readable tree, like a publication that cannot single out a respondent. Weakness: auditors and courts may still demand the original documents on request, and the bank's staff today can freely see the whole file, so the benefit depends on the bank accepting a proof as sufficient evidence under its internal rules and the Financial Supervisory Commission accepting it.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the library policy, a service provider must keep a record of who used what without it becoming a readable log; here, the bank's case file plays that role, and a stored entitlement proof replaces the retained family tree so the record shows the payout basis without being a readable profile.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider must keep a record of who used what without that record becoming a readable log of a person's interests, but the duty is a recommended policy that depends on each institution adopting it and on courts or subpoenas being resisted. | mechanism: Institutional confidentiality policy plus procedures for handling subpoenas and law-enforcement requests; no technical minimization of records is specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the census statute, individual responses are aggregated and nothing may identify a particular respondent; here, the bank's staged-payout ledger plays the aggregate, showing that shares sum to at most 1 without exposing any single heir's relationships.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: An agency holding individual responses must release aggregate results, and the legal duty bars any output from which a particular respondent can be singled out, while the holder's staff can still see the raw records. | mechanism: Statutory use limitation and publication prohibition enforced by sworn-oath duties and penalties; statistical disclosure limitation (for example differential privacy in later census products) is a technical layer not specified in the statute.

title: Spa event or festival bath: crowd entry with attendant-visible result only
moment: At a seasonal open-air hot-spring festival in Wulai, temporary staff at the bath entrance check wristbands and ask guests to show ID so attendants can steer women to the women's area and screen for the tattoo age rule. Many temporary staff handle IDs openly in a queue, and guests' details are seen by passers-by.
verifier: Temporary entrance staff at a festival-run public bath area (contracted event operator)
predicate: Holder is female OR age at or above the tattoo-policy age; staff device shows only a pass/fail and the area (women's / general) to use
disclosed_today: Full ID shown aloud or held up in a public queue: name, birth date, ID number, photo and gender marker visible to staff and bystanders
issuer: Ministry of the Interior (national ID wallet); a local township office may issue a short-lived festival-day credential for residents without the wallet
why_zk: Staff are temporary and not trained in data handling, so reducing what they can see to a pass/fail result limits who can learn identities, similar to a court keeping juror identities confidential by default rather than by judge discretion. Weaknesses: queue speed and wallet adoption among older visitors are real obstacles, and the festival has no legal duty to check, so a paper fallback will remain.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-jury-selection, the identities of those seated are kept from the wider public unless a judge decides otherwise; here, the festival entrance reveals only pass/fail to staff and onlookers, and the verifier app configuration plays the role of the default-confidential rule.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: Someone must be drawn from a pool and seated for a task without the wider public learning who they are, but the default rule can flip to full publication of the identities of everyone selected, with confidentiality only as a judge-level exception. | mechanism: Judge-discretionary confidentiality of juror names under a court's jury selection plan; no technical mechanism specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In an-b-hipaa-min-necessary, the holder of sensitive records releases only the subset serving a stated purpose but nothing proves it was minimal; here, the entrance check releasing only the area decision plays that role, with the ZK proof supplying the missing proof of minimality.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A holder of sensitive records must release only the subset that serves a stated purpose, but the rule leaves it to the holder to judge what is minimal and gives no mechanism that proves the released subset was minimal. | mechanism: Purpose-based minimum-necessary rule with reasonable-efforts standard, role-based access and reasonable reliance on requester representations (45 CFR 164.514(d)); no cryptographic or proof-based check.

title: Public library card upgrade for a member of a community reading cooperative
moment: A resident in Tainan joins a neighborhood book-sharing cooperative that lends from members' shelves and offers priority access to the city library's special collections. To admit new members, the cooperative coordinator asks them to bring a printout of their library account page, which shows current loans and holds, to prove they have no overdue or lost books elsewhere.
predicate: Non-membership: the member is not on the public library network's overdue or lost-item list.
disclosed_today: A screenshot or printout of the library account page with current loans, holds, reading history and fines, plus name and card number.
issuer: The municipal public library, which could sign a standing attestation through its app.
why_zk: Moderate. The volunteer needs no more than a clean-standing result, and a signed non-membership statement avoids handing over a reading history. The honest weakness is that the stakes are low and a volunteer group may simply trust a verbal statement or not care, so adoption depends on the library app offering this with no extra effort.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the ALA guidance, circulation records are confidential and not handed to outsiders; here, the signed clean-standing proof plays that role by keeping the account page away from the cooperative volunteer.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A service provider must keep a record of who used what without that record becoming a readable log of a person's interests, but the duty is a recommended policy that depends on each institution adopting it and on courts or subpoenas being resisted. | mechanism: Institutional confidentiality policy plus procedures for handling subpoenas and law-enforcement requests; no technical minimization of records is specified.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the household register rule, the applicant shows an original for inspection and nothing is retained; here, presenting the credential from the phone plays that role, so the volunteer sees a valid result and keeps no copy.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A person asking an agency for a record must prove identity; the rule specifies inspecting the original card rather than handing over a copy, and it does not say the agency retains anything. | mechanism: Original identity document shown for in-person inspection; the checklist states no retention or copy requirement.
